title: Sprint to launch risk triage and rollout criteria
topics: Risk triage for upcoming private launch
KV cache eviction and quantization rollouts
summary: Team ran a focused risk triage for the private deployment launch. Main concerns: KV cache eviction behavior under concurrent canaries, quantization-induced quality regressions for long-context customers, and FYI on SSO/KMS audit checklist. Decided on three short experiments, a tightened canary criteria set, and an oncall rotation handoff. Action owners assigned and follow-ups scheduled.
action_items: Priya Nair: finalize KV eviction threshold experiment and submit results by 2027-03-14
Sam Ortiz: run 12h canary with synthetic long-context queries, report perf & error spikes by 2027-03-15
Ruth Alvarez: expand regression prompt set to include 6 customer-critical prompts and run nightly evals, first pass due 2027-03-13
Chris Zhang: draft staged degradation runbook and rollback steps, circulate by 2027-03-12
Maya Patel: confirm SOC2 audit evidence locations + KMS integration notes by 2027-03-11
Jordan Meyers: update release checklist with tightened canary criteria and send to execs by 2027-03-11
next_steps: Schedule 2-day canary window next Tuesday 03/16 for high-traffic region
Set a sync with customer success to surface high-impact prompts for regressions
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-03-10 15:00 UTC | Duration 58m | Attendees: Jordan, Priya, Sam, Lena, Chris, Alex, Maya, Oliver, Ruth

Summary: quick run-of triage and go/no-go gating parameters for private deployment. Kinda fast paced, ran through SLOs, quant concerns, KV cache and oncall handoffs.

[00:00] Jordan: ok thanks everyone for joining, I think we have a tight agenda, main goal is to get a list of risks we can mitigate before the private launch and agree on canary gating, so let's be concrete
[00:22] Priya: yep, I'll start with KV cache. We've seen eviction oscillations on long-prefix workloads in perf lab when we bump batch sizes, it shows up as KV cache thrash and token latency spikes
[00:40] Sam: mhm we've seen that too during the last dedup test, the eviction window doesn't respect the pinned prefixes under high concurrency
[01:05] Ruth: and that caused a couple of regressions for the customer test-suite where context-resume failed a few times, so we need to add those into nightly regressions
[01:28] Jordan: action there is to run an eviction threshold sweep and a synthetic 12h concurrency run, Priya and Sam you good to pair?
[01:45] Priya: yeah i'll own the sweep, Sam can set up the traffic generator and the telemetry hooks
[02:10] Alex: one ask from ops — canaries must not be invisible; we need clear signal thresholds otherwise we end up with flapping rollbacks mid-business hours
[02:38] Lena: suggested thresholds? I think we should be explicit: latency p95 increase > 15% AND error rate > 0.5% sustained 10m or token-level regression on eval set
[02:59] Sam: agree but also add KV miss-rate delta > 20% as a gating metric, otherwise latency alone hides cache thrash
[03:20] Chris: on rollout mechanics — we should stage by region and customer tier: first internal, then 10% of low-risk customers, then 50% of low-risk, etc. Need to nail the staged degradation fallback too
[03:45] Priya: this is where quantization comes in. We have two quant profiles: q4_0 and q8_legacy, q4_0 gives 2x cost savings but we saw quality deltas on longer prompts in A/B tests
[04:12] Maya: from security side, quant doesn't change data residency but we need to ensure model artifacts in the private deployment are encrypted with KMS and that audit trails are available for the provable rollouts
[04:35] Jordan: Maya can you confirm KMS mapping and any additional evidence needed for SOC2?
[04:50] Maya: yes, I'll post a checklist in the doc repo; we still need the key rotation policy snapshot and sample audit logs
[05:12] Oliver: ops note — VPC peering for a couple of pilot customers is still pending and that'll affect canary population, need to surface to the account team
[05:30] Jordan: ok add to action items, thanks Oliver

[06:05] -- Mid-call clarification --
[06:20] Ruth: quick point about regressions, when you said 'prompt set' earlier, are we talking about customer ob-eds or internal synthetic ones? We need both, but prioritize customer-critical prompts
[06:44] Priya: correct, Ruth, we'll take 6 high-impact customer prompts and 12 synthetic stress prompts. We'll run nightly evals and flag any model-level deltas > 3% BLEU-ish — yes i know BLEU is not perfect, it's a shorthand for quality delta
[07:10] Jordan: don't get hung up on metric names, just make sure we have actionable thresholds and a human review gate

[07:40] Alex: can we talk about runbook and staged degradation? Last time the fallback to hosted caused state mismatch for session based keys
[07:56] Chris: right, that was because we didn't reconcile kv-cache semantics across hosted/private variants; we need a translation shim or at least a clear invalidation window so session affinity isn't broken
[08:18] Priya: short term fix: strict cache invalidation on model switch and step-down hook that invalidates user session tokens for 30s — not ideal but safer
[08:40] Sam: longer-term: we need a compatibility layer in the runtime that maintains KV key schema across quantized variants

[09:05] Lena: ops question — how long is the canary window recommended? If it's too short we miss tail issues, if too long we block launch schedule
[09:26] Jordan: proposal: 48h internal + 72h low-risk customer step + 7d extended step for broader rollout with rolling telemetry checks. But can be shortened if all gating metrics green and manual signoff
[09:50] Maya: security wants an additional pre-canary smoke: run a dataflow DAG that validates KMS access for the private cluster and a mock audit log ingestion
[10:10] Oliver: that smoke test is quick, we can run it in under an hour if resource keys pre-provisioned

[11:00] -- Timestamps advance (abbreviated for readability) --
[11:15] Priya: experiment plan for KV eviction: sweep thresholds at 5%, 10%, 20% reserve and measure p50/p95 tokens, kv miss rate, and OOM counts
[11:40] Sam: will instrument the runtime counters and add a debug sink, will also run a background kernel fallback to record perf delta
[12:02] Ruth: i'll merge the new prompts into nightly harness and add a flag to fail builds if regression on those prompts beyond threshold
[12:25] Jordan: make sure the nightly doesn't block deploys today; it should be a reporting gate, escalate if we see major deltas

[12:50] Chris: staged degradation runbook — first step: auto-failover to reduced capacity model variant (lighter quant) with explicit user notification and rate-limited throughput
[13:10] Priya: lighter quant tends to increase latency but preserves throughput and keeps costs down, we need to measure UX impact for chat flows
[13:28] Alex: ops: notification needs to include expected degraded behavior, and a ticket auto-created for the incident owner
[13:50] Jordan: add template copy to runbook, Chris will author

[14:20] Maya: security audit note — make sure SSO/SAML assertions for the private control plane are recorded in the audit events, we need sample logs for the auditor
[14:40] Oliver: will add a sidecar to capture assertions during canary windows for 72h sample

[15:05] Priya: question about model routing: do we prefer region-first routing or customer-tier-first? The routing policy affects canary population size and fallback locality
[15:28] Lena: region-first reduces cross-region state problems but customer-tier-first makes it safer for high-value customers
[15:45] Jordan: consensus: region-first for initial canary then customer-tier for the 2nd step; we'll document the policy in the rollout plan

[16:12] Ruth: quick QA note — need a plan for fuzz tests that simulate partial KV corruption, that surfaced a tricky recovery path last quarter
[16:30] Priya: good call, add a fuzz test to the nightly harness and include corruption scenarios at 1% and 5% of keys

[17:02] -- Decision moment --
[17:18] Jordan: ok decisions so far: 1) run KV sweep + 12h concurrency canary; 2) tighten canary gating to include KV miss-rate delta; 3) staged rollout steps set to 48h/72h/7d; 4) security pre-canary smoke mandatory. Any objections?
[17:40] Maya: none from security assuming I get the KMS evidence by Friday
[17:55] Chris: no objections from release team, will draft runbook and a rollback checklist

[18:15] Alex: one more ops ask — reserve capacity for canary so we don't affect production pools, otherwise we'll be chasing noise
[18:34] Sam: yes will provision an isolated canary pool and also enable detailed tracing for first 24h

[19:00] -- Closing section: schedule & handoff --
[19:12] Jordan: handoff to oncall: Sam you'll be primary for the canary window, Alex is ops liaison, Ruth will own regression alerts, Chris will handle rollback steps; Jordan will coordinate exec comms
[19:36] Sam: acknowledged, i'll post the rotation and escalation matrix to slack #launch-runbook and tag the oncall
[19:58] Ruth: will add the QA checklists to the doc and ensure nightly evals run before canary starts
[20:20] Priya: i'll pair with Sam early next week to validate telemetry hooks and KV counters

[20:45] Jordan: final — we should capture any follow-up links here. Deck: https://drive.google.com/rd-launch/kv-quant-triage-deck (internal). Runbook draft: docs.redwood/internal/staged-degrade-runbook.md. SOC2 pack: docs.redwood/internal/soc2-launch-pack. Canary spreadsheet: sheets.redwood/internal/canary-population.xlsx

[21:12] -- Wrap and quick Q&A --
[21:25] Oliver: timeline check — if we hit all green on experiments this week, are we still on track for the 03/22 private launch?
[21:40] Jordan: yes conditional — green experiments and no critical regressions. If a major regression appears we'll delay by one week to get fixes and a second canary window
[22:04] Maya: auditor scheduling — i'll schedule a quick 30m pre-audit check with the compliance team on 03/12
[22:20] Jordan: great. Thanks everyone. Meeting adjourned.

Note: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings (e.g., quant names q4_0 transcribed as q four oh) and speaker overlaps. Decks and spreadsheets referenced above were shared in chat during call.
